headline: High risk of capability conflict and cascading errors: OpenHands can write/run tools in a shared runtime while LlamaFactory has no runtime isolation or execution surfaces documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no filesystem, clipboard, stdin/stdout, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest B’s outputs by default. B can read/write runtime files and use MCP, so prompt injection is only plausible if an operator manually bridges content into B’s workspace or tools. The pathway is unusual and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-generated text into B’s runtime files or MCP inputs
IF B is configured to treat mounted file content as instructions
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces
Do not paste A outputs into B prompts or files
Disable MCP servers for B unless needed
Use a read-only handoff file for any transfer
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred content

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no read or write surfaces, while B only touches files mounted into its runtime. There is no documented shared workspace or outbound exfiltration path from A. Leakage becomes plausible only if sensitive files are mounted into B and then manually copied into A-related workflows, so the blast radius is constrained.
conditions: IF sensitive files are mounted into B’s runtime
IF those files are then exported or copied into another system
mitigations: Mount only non-sensitive files in B
Rotate or redact secrets before mounting
Review B runtime mounts before launch
Keep A disconnected from any shared workspace
requires-engineering: enforce per-file access controls on mounts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and git modification inside its runtime, while A is non-runnable and has no write or git capabilities. The conflict is not symmetric, but B’s default write-heavy behavior can still collide with any shared mounted volume or repo state. Uncertainty about the exact shared path should be resolved upward.
conditions: IF A and B are pointed at the same mounted volume or repository
IF B performs git or filesystem writes without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate directories to A and B
Pause B before any shared-volume write
Use git branches per agent
Add a lock file around shared resources
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level write serialization

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is not runnable and produces no documented outputs, but B can act on files and shell commands in its runtime. If A’s generated text is manually fed into B, B may treat it as authoritative unless the operator verifies it. The pathway exists in non-default handoff workflows, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF A output is manually copied into B as task context
IF B is instructed to execute actions based on unverified text
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A output
Use a checklist for any handoff
Ask B to cite source files before acting
Limit B to read-only analysis mode for the handoff
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: A is open-source docs-only with no data classes or residency claims, while B handles files mounted into its runtime and may use third-party model providers. No specific residency or certification mismatch is documented between them, so only a low compliance concern remains from possible operator-chosen data placement. The other agent is not cited for a specific violation because none is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is mounted into B’s runtime
IF B is configured to send prompts or files to a third-party model provider
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in B mounts
Use a provider with an approved DPA
Review retention settings before launch
Keep audit logs of transferred files
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
